intervention_label: Pembrolizumab + carboplatin/gemcitabine (KEYNOTE-355 backbone) — gated on 22C3 CPS >=10
expected_benefit: In the PD-L1 CPS >=10 stratum: PFS HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.49-0.86; mPFS 9.7 vs 5.6 mo) and final OS HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.55-0.95; mOS 23.0 vs 16.1 mo). A gemcitabine/carboplatin backbone also delivers the platinum her BRCA1 tumor is doubly sensitive to (TNT BRCA-mut subset ORR 68% vs 33%).
key_risks: Grade 3+ treatment-related AEs 68.1% (vs 66.9% chemo alone), driven by the gem/carbo backbone (G3+ neutropenia ~41%)
Grade 3+ immune-mediated AEs 5.3% — hypothyroidism, hepatitis, pneumonitis
Treatment-related deaths 0.4%
In an MSS tumor, a B2M/HLA class I-loss subclone would blunt the checkpoint half despite the favorable TMB/TIL signal
preference_alignment: matches efficacy lean (0.7): YES — highest-floor 1L survival evidence. matches prefers_trials: PARTIAL — off-trial as written, but this exact backbone is the control arm of the recruiting TROPION-Breast05 (rank 5), so enrolling there delivers the same floor on-protocol. no toxicity_vetoes or modality_constraints to breach.
guideline_status: NCCN Breast v4.2025 category 1 / preferred and ESMO class I for 1L mTNBC with 22C3 CPS >=10.
rationale_summary: All five personas ranked this among their top four and none dissented or vetoed, giving it the only unanimous-endorsement agreement score in the case. It is the 1L regimen with the maturest survival evidence in metastatic TNBC (final OS at 44-month follow-up), and the carboplatin flavor of the backbone serves the BRCA1 axis at the same time. The load-bearing condition, named by every persona, is that the labeled benefit lives entirely in the 22C3 CPS >=10 stratum, and CPS is pending — the favorable TMB-14 and 3+ TIL phenotype does not rescue a CPS-low result, since the label tracks CPS, not those surrogates. The critic added that even here the PARP axis carries two independent registered phase-3 hits against KEYNOTE-355's one, so if germline BRCA1 resolves before CPS returns, replication count argues the PARP monotherapy could lead. The advocate and concensusite both pushed the trials-first framing: this backbone is TROPION-Breast05's control arm, so the on-protocol route reproduces it.
open_questions: PD-L1 CPS by 22C3 on the breast primary is pending and gates the entire regimen; primary-vs-liver-met discordance runs 20-30%
Sequencing against the PARP axis in a gBRCA CPS-high patient is unsettled by guidelines
likelihood_of_effect: High in the CPS >=10 subset: OS HR 0.73 / mOS 23.0 vs 16.1 mo (pmid:35857659); zero labeled benefit if CPS returns <10, and CPS is pending.

counter_productive_moa.description: In an MSS tumor a B2M/HLA class I-loss subclone would blunt the checkpoint arm, but no persona vetoed on mechanism.

overall: **The maturest 1L survival evidence in mTNBC and the board's only unanimous endorsement, though the entire labeled benefit is gated on a pending CPS >=10 result.**

intervention_label: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID (OlympiAD) — gated on germline BRCA1 confirmation
expected_benefit: OlympiAD: PFS HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.43-0.80; mPFS 7.0 vs 4.2 mo), ORR 59.9% vs 28.8%. Oral, single-agent, chemo-free. OlympiA adjuvant data (n=1836) extends the safety window with no MDS/AML excess at 300 mg BID.
key_risks: Grade 3+ anemia 16.1% — the dominant AE; set a transfusion/hold threshold before starting
Grade 3+ AE rate 36.6% overall (below the 50.5% comparator chemo)
Cumulative MDS/AML ~1-2% across the pooled PARP dataset over a 12-18 month horizon
preference_alignment: matches efficacy lean (0.7): PARTIAL — single-agent PARPi is less aggressive than ICI+chemo in 1L but fits an oral, curative-adjacent bridge. matches prefers_trials: PARTIAL — off-trial standard, though it is the maintenance answer after a platinum induction. no toxicity_veto or modality_constraint breached.
guideline_status: NCCN Breast v4.2025 category 1 and ESMO class I for gBRCA1/2 HER2-negative mBC — but only while BRCA1 reads germline; somatic-only moves it off-label.
rationale_summary: Four personas ranked olaparib (the critic and concensusite at rank 1, the conservative at rank 2, the advocate at rank 3); no persona dissented or vetoed. It is anchored on two independent registrational phase-3 RCTs (OlympiAD and EMBRACA) in exactly this indication, the evidence bar the critic and concensusite both weight above every abstract-level DDR agent in the dossier. Between the two labeled PARP inhibitors the conservative, concensusite and advocate all favor olaparib over talazoparib on the hematologic margin (G3+ anemia 16.1% vs 39%). The load-bearing gate is germline-vs-somatic BRCA1: the FDA breast label and the category-1 statement are germline-restricted, so a somatic-only call moves this off-label, at which point the Stanford somatic-talazoparib trial (NCT03990896) becomes the on-axis route. The advocate's only reservation was preference-flavored — with prefers_trials true she would foreground the enrollable options first — not a dissent on the drug.
open_questions: Germline-vs-somatic BRCA1 is unresolved on tumor NGS and gates the labeled indication
A baseline ctDNA draw before any PARP exposure is worth having, since BRCA1 reversion is the dominant later resistance route
likelihood_of_effect: High in gBRCA1 disease: PFS HR 0.58, ORR 60% (pmid:28578601), replicated by EMBRACA; off-label and weaker-supported if BRCA1 is somatic-only.

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism blunts the therapeutic goal; later BRCA1 reversion is a resistance route, not a counter-productive vector.

overall: **Category-1, replicated, oral single-agent efficacy directly on the BRCA1 axis with the gentlest hematologic profile of the PARP options — conditional on the germline call.**

intervention_label: Talazoparib 1 mg PO daily (EMBRACA) — gated on germline BRCA1 confirmation
expected_benefit: EMBRACA: PFS HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41-0.71; mPFS 8.6 vs 5.6 mo), ORR 62.6% vs 27.2% — the deepest single-agent response rate on the BRCA1 axis. OS was not significantly improved (HR 0.76, p=0.11). If BRCA1 is somatic-only, the Stanford NCT03990896 somatic cohort showed ~38% ORR.
key_risks: Grade 3+ anemia ~39% — substantially heavier than olaparib; likely dose holds or transfusion support
Grade 3+ neutropenia ~21%, thrombocytopenia ~15%
Same germline-restricted label as olaparib
preference_alignment: matches efficacy lean (0.7): YES — the risktaker's rank 1, chasing the deepest response to convert the liver lesion to an ablation candidate. matches prefers_trials: PARTIAL. no toxicity_veto set, so the heavier anemia does not breach a stated constraint.
guideline_status: NCCN Breast v4.2025 category 1 and ESMO class I for gBRCA1/2 HER2-negative mBC, equal-labeled with olaparib; germline-gated.
rationale_summary: All five personas endorsed talazoparib as a PARP option and none dissented, though they split on ordering relative to olaparib: the risktaker ranked it 1 for the highest PARP-trapping potency and the deepest ORR (62.6%), while the conservative, critic and advocate placed it just below olaparib purely on the hematologic-tolerability delta. The efficacy is not in question — EMBRACA is a mature registrational RCT at parity with OlympiAD. The gap between rank 2 and rank 3 is tolerability, not evidence: talazoparib's G3+ anemia (~39% vs 16.1%) spends more marrow reserve for a patient who may also need myelosuppressive chemo before or after. The risktaker's conversion argument — a deep response making the solitary hepatic lesion resectable — is the reason it stays a legitimate co-lead rather than dropping. Same germline gate as olaparib; somatic-only routes through the Stanford trial.
open_questions: Germline-vs-somatic BRCA1 gates the label identically to olaparib
Whether the deeper ORR converts the liver lesion to a local-therapy candidate is the curative-intent hypothesis, testable only on-protocol (rank 9)
likelihood_of_effect: High in gBRCA1 disease: PFS HR 0.54, ORR 62.6% (pmid:30110579) — deepest single-agent response; OS gain not significant.

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism-level counter-productive vector; the risktaker/critic split was on tolerability and ORR depth, not mechanism.

overall: **Equal-labeled PARP alternative with the deepest ORR on the BRCA1 axis; ranks below olaparib only on a heavier hematologic burden, not on evidence.**

intervention_label: Carboplatin AUC2 + gemcitabine d1,8 q21d (PD-L1-agnostic, germline-agnostic BRCA1 backbone)
expected_benefit: TNT BRCA-mut subset (n=43): carboplatin ORR 68.0% vs 33.3% docetaxel, PFS HR 0.44 (mPFS 6.8 vs 4.4 mo; interaction p=0.01). BrighTNess/CALGB 40603 confirm the platinum, not the added PARP, drives depth of response. Doubles as the induction backbone for a later olaparib or PARP+IO maintenance.
key_risks: Additive myelosuppression from the doublet — G3+ neutropenia 30-40%, thrombocytopenia ~15%; day-8 counts drive dose modification
Well-characterized, dose-modifiable, standard supportive-care algorithms apply
Gives up the OS advantage the pembrolizumab arm carries if CPS >=10 returns
preference_alignment: matches efficacy lean (0.7): PARTIAL — a cytotoxic doublet is the floor, not the ceiling. matches prefers_trials: NO — off-trial standard. Its value is that it cannot be gated out from under the patient by either pending biomarker.
guideline_status: NCCN Breast v4.2025 category 1 / preferred platinum backbone for 1L mTNBC, with explicit BRCA-mut support; NCCN Compendium covers the indication.
rationale_summary: Three personas (conservative rank 3, critic rank 5, concensusite rank 3) endorsed the platinum doublet; none dissented or vetoed. Its rank sits on a specific role rather than headline efficacy: it is the one 1L option that works regardless of how the CPS and germline questions resolve, so it cannot be gated out from under the patient. The BRCA1 platinum-sensitivity evidence is direct (TNT), but the personas are candid that the BRCA-mut readout is an n=43 pre-specified subgroup with a wide CI, not a registrational 1L anchor — class evidence plus decades of post-marketing experience. It ranks below the PARP options because it gives up the chemo-free footprint and the replicated RCT tier, and below pembro+chemo because it forgoes the OS advantage in a CPS-high patient. It is the defensible hold if both biomarker gates close, and the induction platform for a PARP or PARP+IO maintenance strategy (DORA/KEYLYNK-009 template).
open_questions: The BRCA-mut carboplatin advantage rests on a small pre-specified subgroup extrapolated to the 1L de novo setting
No registrational 1L OS data for carbo/gem specifically in PD-L1-low BRCA1-mut mTNBC
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate-to-high in BRCA1-mut disease: ORR 68% vs 33% for carboplatin over taxane (pmid:29713086), from an n=43 subgroup with a wide CI.

counter_productive_moa.description: No counter-productive mechanism; the tradeoff is forgone OS benefit versus the CPS-gated ICI arm, not a mechanistic vector.

overall: **The biomarker-agnostic BRCA1 platinum backbone that no pending test can foreclose; a floor and an induction platform rather than the efficacy ceiling.**

intervention_label: Datopotamab deruxtecan +/- durvalumab on TROPION-Breast05 (NCT06103864) — 1L on-protocol route if CPS >=10
expected_benefit: Readout pending. The recruiting 1L pivotal randomizes Dato-DXd +/- durvalumab against the KEYNOTE-355 backbone in CPS >=10 mTNBC, so the control arm reproduces the rank-1 standard-of-care floor; the experimental arms add a TROP2-ADC targeting the basal feature plus a durvalumab arm leveraging the TMB-H / TIL-rich phenotype.
key_risks: Class Dato-DXd AEs: stomatitis, ocular events, and ILD/pneumonitis (~3% any-grade, the characteristic deruxtecan-payload signal)
1:1 randomization risks assignment to the control arm — the same gem/carbo+pembro obtainable off-trial
No BRCA1 synthetic-lethal mechanism, so the experimental arm spends the curative-intent window on TROP2 rather than the DDR axis
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES — the recruiting on-axis 1L trial the preference file reads as written for. matches efficacy lean (0.7): YES via the experimental TROP2-ADC + ICI arm. no toxicity_veto or modality_constraint breached.
guideline_status: Investigational in 1L mTNBC — no NCCN category or ESMO recommendation for Dato-DXd here; the guideline-aligned framing is enrollment, with KEYNOTE-355 as the standard the control arm reproduces.
rationale_summary: The advocate ranked this first as the trial the preference file was effectively written for: recruiting, 1L, on-axis, gated on the same pending CPS, with a control arm that bounds the downside at standard of care. Two personas dissented and neither the biology nor the guideline supports it as a lead. The risktaker's dissent is mechanistic: a 1:1 randomization can assign her to the control arm, and Dato-DXd carries no BRCA1 synthetic-lethal mechanism, so it spends her curative-intent window on TROP2 rather than the DDR axis that could actually shrink the liver lesion. The concensusite's dissent is on guideline fit: putting an investigational ADC at rank 1 over the category-1 CPS >=10 standard inverts the evidence hierarchy — enrollment is honored by ranking the trial as the vehicle, not as proof Dato-DXd outranks KEYNOTE-355. Because the advocate flagged it preference-aligned while two personas dissented, it lands as considered_with_caveats: a legitimate on-protocol route to the same floor plus an experimental ceiling, not a first-line efficacy claim.
open_questions: Readout is pending; there is no efficacy estimate for the experimental arms yet
CPS <10 removes eligibility and shifts the on-protocol route to TROPION-Breast02 or TroFuse-011
Randomization to the control arm delivers standard of care, not the experimental TROP2-ADC
likelihood_of_effect: Unquantified: 1L pivotal readout pending (nct:NCT06103864); the control arm reproduces the KEYNOTE-355 floor, the experimental-arm benefit is untested.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (stomatitis, ocular events, ILD/pneumonitis; fewer hematologic events than chemo)

counter_productive_moa.description: TROP2-ADC has no DDR mechanism, so the experimental arm may spend the curative-intent window off the BRCA1 axis (risktaker dissent).

overall: **The recruiting 1L on-protocol route whose control arm reproduces standard of care, honoring the trials-first preference; the experimental arm's TROP2 mechanism sits off the BRCA1 axis and is untested.**

expected_benefit: TOPACIO: cohort-level ORR 21% (95% CI 12-33, n=42); the headline 47% is the BRCA-mut TNBC subgroup (n=15). The chemo-free PARP+PD-1 pairing is mechanistically matched to her BRCA1 + TMB-14 + 3+ TIL phenotype; MEDIOLA (olaparib+durvalumab) points the same way (ORR 63%, DCR 80%, n=34).
key_risks: Overlapping hematologic burden: G3+ anemia 18%, thrombocytopenia 15%, plus immune-related AEs (15% any-grade, 4% G3+)
Niraparib is off-label in breast cancer with no NCCN Compendium support — payer denial likely versus labeled olaparib/talazoparib
No dedicated combination safety readout in TNBC; the AE algorithm for the doublet does not exist the way it does for labeled PARP monotherapy
preference_alignment: matches efficacy lean (0.7): YES on ceiling — a chemo-free high-ORR bet. matches prefers_trials: PARTIAL — TOPACIO is completed; the enrollable analog is a PARP+IO maintenance design after platinum induction (DORA/KEYLYNK-009), not this exact regimen.
guideline_status: Not NCCN- or ESMO-endorsed in breast cancer; niraparib is off-label with no compendium support, so payer access is the practical bottleneck.
rationale_summary: The risktaker ranked this third on its high ceiling; the critic dissented and the conservative attached a heavy toxicity qualifier, so it sits at neutral agreement and considered_with_caveats. The 47% ORR the pick leans on is an n=15 BRCA-mut subgroup, and the published cohort-level number is 21% across n=42 with a confidence interval wide enough to swallow much of the enthusiasm — a single-arm signal with no comparator to apportion credit between the PARP inhibitor, the checkpoint, and BRCA1 selection. The biology, a neoantigen-generating PARP inhibitor stacked on a checkpoint that exploits them, is a reasonable prior for this exact phenotype, which is why it stays on the list, but the evidence does not carry it above the replicated category-1 backbones for a treatment-naive patient. The realistic home for the chemo-free PARP+IO concept is a maintenance strategy after platinum induction, not a front-line move; niraparib's off-label status adds a payer hurdle that labeled olaparib/talazoparib avoid.
open_questions: The 47% rests on n=15; a larger cohort would likely regress toward the published 21%
No TNBC-specific combination safety readout exists for the doublet
The enrollable form is a PARP+IO maintenance design after platinum, not this completed trial
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate but uncertain: BRCA-mut subgroup ORR 47% (n=15) vs published cohort 21% (n=42, pmid:31194225); single-arm, no comparator.

counter_productive_moa.description: In an MSS tumor a B2M/HLA-loss subclone would blunt the checkpoint half; critic dissented on the thin single-arm evidence base.

overall: **A mechanistically clean chemo-free PARP+IO bet for this exact BRCA1/TMB/TIL phenotype, but the 47% is an n=15 subgroup and niraparib is off-label — a later-line maintenance question, not a 1L move.**

intervention_label: PARP1-selective inhibitor trial — HS-10502 on NCT05740956 (saruparib/PETRA as class precedent), later-line
expected_benefit: Saruparib PETRA breast subset (n=31 at 60 mg): ORR 48.4% (95% CI 35.7-61.3), mPFS 9.1 mo, with less hematologic toxicity than approved PARP1/2 inhibitors. PARP1-selectivity aims to spare the anemia/thrombocytopenia that cap olaparib and talazoparib. HS-10502 has a dedicated HRR-mutant HER2-negative breast cohort her BRCA1 status matches.
key_risks: HS-10502 has no published efficacy or safety readout of its own — the 48.4% ORR belongs to saruparib and is abstract-level
The saruparib breast subset pooled HR+ and TNBC, so the TNBC-specific ORR could be lower; no per-term G3+ table released
Enrollment is 2L+ with a prior-therapy expectation, so a treatment-naive patient needs a first line before qualifying
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES — a recruiting on-axis breast cohort. matches efficacy lean (0.7): PARTIAL on an abstract-level signal. The toxicity-sparing rationale aligns with the efficacy-leaning-but-liveable spirit of the 0.7 weight even with no toxicity_veto set.
guideline_status: Investigational — no NCCN category or ESMO score. The guideline-aligned route is enrollment, not off-label prescribing.
rationale_summary: The board split three-to-two. The risktaker, concensusite and advocate surfaced the PARP1-selective class as a preference-aligned trial option, toxicity-sparing for a young patient facing years on the DDR axis; the conservative and critic dissented on evidence quality. The dissents are precise and persist regardless of biomarker status: the 48.4% ORR is a single-arm AACR abstract with a mixed HR+/TNBC subset, a null PMID, and no per-term grade-3+ table, so the toxicity-sparing claim is a mechanistic hypothesis a trial is meant to test, not a characterized profile — and HS-10502, the actually-enrollable agent, has no readout of its own and must not inherit saruparib's number. Every persona who surfaced it agreed it does not outrank the replicated category-1 PARP RCTs and belongs 2L+, after a first line. It stays ranked because the enrollable form is a legitimate on-protocol route for the toxicity-sparing bet, not because the efficacy is established.
open_questions: HS-10502's own efficacy and safety are unpublished; the class number is cross-subtype abstract data
The TNBC-specific PARP1-selective ORR is unknown
2L+ enrollment means it sits after a first line, not at presentation
likelihood_of_effect: Uncertain: class-precedent ORR 48.4% (saruparib PETRA, abstract, mixed HR+/TNBC); HS-10502's own activity unpublished.
toxicity_burden: Not characterized (per-term G3+ table not released; mechanism predicts less anemia)

counter_productive_moa.description: Critic and conservative dissented on the unproven toxicity-sparing claim; no per-term safety data to confirm PARP1-selectivity spares marrow.

overall: **The enrollable toxicity-sparing PARP bet for a young patient facing years on the DDR axis, but the efficacy is cross-subtype abstract-level and the enrollable agent has no readout of its own.**

intervention_label: Olaparib + ceralasertib (ATR-i) on the recruiting germline-BRCA arm (NCT04090567) — later-line
expected_benefit: plasmaMATCH Cohort E: TNBC-specific ORR 17.1% (95% CI 10.4-25.5, n=70), with responses in HRR-wildtype and functional-HRD tumors that fit her BRCA1 + TP53 replication-stress phenotype. The MD Anderson trial gives the ATR combination a recruiting germline-BRCA home.
key_risks: VIOLETTE, the dedicated randomized test, showed the combination did not beat olaparib monotherapy (PFS HR ~0.81, NS)
Adds anemia and hypertension over single-agent olaparib
Setting mismatch — Cohort E is 2L+ pretreated; a 17% ORR does not transfer to 1L treatment-naive disease, and washout makes it non-1L-enrollable
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES — recruiting, on-axis for BRCA1 + TP53. matches efficacy lean (0.7): PARTIAL — modest ORR, later-line. no veto or modality breach.
guideline_status: Investigational — not NCCN- or ESMO-endorsed; VIOLETTE was negative for the combination over olaparib alone.
rationale_summary: The critic (rank 4) and advocate (rank 4) both surfaced this as the best-evidenced of the new DDR-combination entries — plasmaMATCH Cohort E is a genuinely published, TNBC-specific cohort, unlike the abstract-only POLtheta/PARG rows — while being candid about its ceiling. The conservative's qualifier, which reads as a dissent on incremental value, is that the ATR combination buys unproven incremental efficacy over the PARP monotherapy she is already eligible for: Cohort E is a single-arm 17% ORR, and the one randomized trial built to prove the concept (VIOLETTE) failed to beat olaparib alone. Both the setting mismatch, 2L+ pretreated versus her 1L treatment-naive disease, and the washout requirement make it non-enrollable now. It ranks here as a recruiting later-line trial slot with a documented anemia/hypertension monitoring plan, not a 1L move and not a substitute for the labeled PARP monotherapy above it.
open_questions: The combination's incremental value over PARP monotherapy is unproven by the one randomized trial designed to test it
Cohort E's 17% ORR is 2L+ and does not transfer to the front line
Washout requirements make it non-1L-enrollable for a treatment-naive patient
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate: TNBC ORR 17.1% (pmid:37773077), single-arm 2L+; the randomized VIOLETTE test did not beat olaparib alone.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (anemia and hypertension added over single-agent olaparib)

counter_productive_moa.description: Conservative flagged that the added ATR toxicity buys efficacy the randomized trial could not demonstrate over PARP monotherapy.

overall: **The best-evidenced DDR-combination entry and a recruiting home for the BRCA1+TP53 ATR rationale, but VIOLETTE was negative over olaparib alone and it is 2L+ only.**

intervention_label: SBRT to the solitary liver lesion as consolidation on the MSK SABR trial (NCT05534438) — trial-only, after systemic response
expected_benefit: The MSK randomized phase 2 enrolls de novo oligometastatic breast disease and lets her get SBRT on-protocol once a 12-week scan confirms the breast and axilla are controlled — the on-trial route to test whether ablating the solitary 1.5 cm hepatic lesion converts the curative-intent framing into a durable outcome. Layers on the systemic backbone; never replaces it.
key_risks: NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS favored systemic therapy alone (HR ~1.31); routine off-protocol SBRT consolidation is not supported
E2108 found no OS benefit from local therapy of the intact primary (OS HR 1.11)
The curative-intent rationale rests on biology selection of a single small lesion, not a positive randomized signal
preference_alignment: matches curative-intent free_text: YES — the reason it appears on a 1L list at all. matches prefers_trials: YES — the MSK slot is the on-protocol route rather than off-protocol ablation. Consolidation only, layered on the systemic picks above.
guideline_status: Not guideline-endorsed as routine practice — NCCN does not endorse routine oligometastatic SBRT consolidation after NRG-BR002; a case-by-case tumor-board decision, framed here as trial-only.
rationale_summary: The advocate ranked this fifth on the strength of the patient's explicit curative-intent free_text and the fact that a solitary 1.5 cm hepatic lesion is the most consolidatable disease she will ever present with; no persona dissented or vetoed, but the advocate carried the counter-evidence herself and the conservative and critic both flagged that off-protocol local therapy is unsupported. The load-bearing point, which the advocate conceded to the critic in round 2, is that both randomized trials point against consolidation for unselected patients (NRG-BR002 PFS HR 1.31; E2108 OS HR 1.11) — which is precisely why the recommendation is the MSK trial slot rather than off-protocol ablation. It is consolidation, not systemic therapy: only defensible layered on top of the systemic backbone after a documented response, and it stays at the bottom of the ranking because it neither targets the tumor biology directly nor rests on a positive randomized signal.
open_questions: Whether biology-selected single-lesion consolidation escapes the negative unselected-patient randomized signal is the open trial question
Requires a documented systemic response first, so timing is downstream of the rank 1-4 decision
likelihood_of_effect: Low for durable benefit off-protocol: randomized consolidation was negative in unselected patients (NRG-BR002 HR 1.31, pmid:33885704); trial-only, biology-selected.
toxicity_burden: Low (radiation modality; lesion-specific, no systemic AE profile)

counter_productive_moa.description: No mechanism blunts the systemic goal; the risk is null benefit from consolidation, per the negative randomized readouts.

overall: **The on-protocol route to the curative-intent framing the patient asked for, honestly tempered by two negative randomized consolidation trials — a trial-only layer on the systemic backbone, never a standalone.**
